calls.reasoning: In July Apple guided Sep-quarter (Q4 FY26) revenue at +9-11% YoY on $102.466B, which is about $111.7-113.7B. That guide already includes a 2.5pt FX headwind and supply limits that Apple said would increase significantly. Consensus is about $113.3B (+10.6%). In FY26 Apple has landed at or above the top of its guide, and the last 7 quarters beat consensus by a median of about 0.6%. That puts my median around $113.9B (+11.2%). Hard supply limits and slower Services growth cap the upside. The reported iPhone 18 Pro order cuts are mostly for October, so they fall in the December quarter. Results under $112B would mean coming in below the guided low end, which Apple rarely does by that much (Q4 FY25 missed its low end by only ~0.1pt). I price that at about 8%. Above $118B would need more than 15% growth, which a supply-constrained guide makes unlikely, so about 2%. I found no human market on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers, and the runs found none either.
calls.reconciliation: All three dossiers agree on the facts: the Nov 2 report date, the $102.466B prior-year base, the +9-11% guide with FX and supply caveats, consensus of about $113.3B, and no prediction market. Only run 3 cited the iPhone 18 Pro order cuts. They concern October, so I judged them mostly a December-quarter issue with little effect on Q4. The disagreements are matters of judgment: the median ($113.7-114.0B) and the lower-escape mass (5-14%). Apple's FY26 record of hitting the top of its guide supports a median just above consensus. Run 1's 14% chance of landing below $112B (under the guided midpoint-to-low area) is too high: a sub-9.3% result would be a miss below the low end, and Apple's recent misses below the low end have been tiny. Run 2's 5% looks slightly low given the supply and memory uncertainty. I carried forward runs 1 and 3's dispersion. I had no web access on this run.
